subject: Implementation: batch/window/quant guidance for ACME AI
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@acme.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T11:08:00-05:00
Subject: Performance knobs question for Redwood implementation

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier — our engineering lead asked me to follow up with some specifics so we can map implementation effort to measurable outcomes. Short background: we run an in-product assistant (chat-first) with median request length ~60 tokens, p95 around 220 tokens. We need to target p95 user-observed latency <= 350ms and reduce inference spend by ~30% vs our current hosted provider.

Three areas we'd like pragmatic guidance on as part of the initial deployment:
- Batching: recommended batch window / max batch size for steady-state vs bursty traffic? Any guidance on micro-batching tradeoffs for interactive UX.
- Caching: whether prefix/KV caching will help given we have a small set of repeated system prompts and a handful (~10) high-frequency user prompts. Also TTL suggestions.
- Quantization & routing: recommended quant profiles to hit the cost target without quality regressions, and routing policy (fast quantized model primary + higher-quality fallback?) suggestions.

We can share a 24-hour sample of traffic if that helps. Could you put together a short, prioritized implementation plan we can hand to our SREs?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Li
Head of Integrations, Acme AI
Anna@acme.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-16T09:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Performance knobs question for Redwood implementation

Hi Anna — great questions, thanks for the clarity. Below is a pragmatic, prioritized plan you can hand to SRE/Platform for the first-phase rollout. I kept it prescriptive so your engineers have concrete knobs to try in the first 72 hours.

Summary recommendations (short):
1) Baseline micro-batching: batch window 20–30ms, max_batch_requests 8, max_batch_tokens 2048. Start with 25ms and monitor p95; increase to 40ms only if p95 remains under target.
2) KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for system prompts + top-10 repeated prompts. TTL: 10s for conversational state, 300s for static system prompts.
3) Quantization profile & canary: primary: q4_0 on redwood-rt-13b (quantized int4 path) for cost baseline; reserve q8_0 or fp16 on a secondary pool for fallback/QA. Canary rollout: 5% -> 20% over 72h, compare semantic-quality metrics on heldout prompt set.
4) Routing policy: primary: latency-weighted routing to same-region quantized pool; fallback: cross-region higher-precision model if latency budget exceeded or quality regression detected. Implement automatic fallback threshold at +25% error-rate-on-evals or p95 > 1.5x target.

Implementation checklist (first cut):
- Instrument: token-level cost per request, per-route p50/p95, sample outputs for quality drift detection.
- Batching config: set initial batch_window_ms=25, max_batch_requests=8, max_batch_tokens=2048. Enable adaptive batching to collapse partial batches during idle windows.
- Cache: configure prefix_kv:true, ttl_system=300s, ttl_conversation=10s, warmup heuristic: prefetch kv for top-50 active users on ramp-up.
- Quant profiles: enable q4_0 profile on dedicated pool, prepare q8_0 for QA validation. See attached quant_profiles.csv for performance/quality deltas we've observed in similar apps.
- Routing: create a policy named "acme-prod-primary" with weights: primary=0.85, fallback=0.15; canary policy "acme-quant-canary" starting at 5%.
- Rollout plan: day 0 deploy q4_0 at 2% traffic (if risk-averse) or 5% otherwise; day 1 -> 10%; day 2 -> 20% observing quality/regressions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Cold-start p95 spike: pre-warm KV cache during ramp with synthetic warmup calls and set a short initial warm-up batch window (50ms) for first 10 minutes.
- Output quality drift under q4_0 on some prompts: keep "mute-redirect" to high-precision fallback and maintain rolling evaluation on the 100-prompt sentinel set.

Next steps I can own:
- Send a short implementation checklist PDF you can attach in your internal ticket (attached).
- Run a 30-minute tuning workshop with your SREs to walk through telemetry dashboards and sample traffic. Proposed times: 2026-12-21 10:00 or 15:00 EST.

If that works I'll also upload the suggested initial dashboards and a pre-workshop checklist.

Best,
Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-17T08:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Performance knobs question for Redwood implementation

Looping in quickly — adding two operational checks before the workshop:

1) Observability: make sure the telemetry includes token-level cost, per-route p50/p95, and a per-prompt quality flag (binary) so we can compute false-positive regressions quickly. We'll provide a Grafana dashboard template in the drive link above.
2) Canary aggressiveness: if Acme prefers conservative rollout, shift canary start from 5% to 2% and extend ramp period to 5 days at smaller increments (2% -> 5% -> 10% -> 20%). That approach costs a bit more in coordination time but greatly reduces user-visible regressions.

Monica — can you add a short pre-workshop checklist for their SREs (ports to open, required IAM role, sample curl to simulate warmup)? I'll join the tuning workshop.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
